fichas.title: Sound insulation: airborne transmission and secondary paths
fichas.summary: Explains airborne sound transmission through building elements, the influence of boundary frequency, and the reduction in insulation caused by secondary-path transmission. Notes that party walls should have substantial surface mass and that doors and windows can strongly affect overall insulation.
spaces: Party walls between flats or houses
uses: Limit airborne sound transmission between buildings and occupied spaces
Account for secondary-path transmission when evaluating sound insulation

fichas.title: Sound insulation of doors and windows
fichas.summary: Compares stated sound-insulation limits for door and window configurations. The text emphasizes that openings can reduce the insulation of a wall and that improving their sound insulation may be a priority.

uses: Compare sound-insulation values of door and window arrangements

fichas.title: Minimum sound-insulation requirements for occupied rooms
fichas.summary: Table excerpt gives airborne and impact sound-insulation values for separating elements in multi-storey residential and mixed-use buildings, schools, and accommodation or healthcare settings. The stated partitioning-element values include the effects of materials and secondary paths in the installed condition; door values apply only to transmission through the door.
